alt: A table that gains a row each time n doubles. The single loop's operation count doubles every time, while the nested pairs loop's count grows by a factor that settles close to four.

steps.caption: At n = 100 a single loop does 100 operations and the pairs loop does 4,950. Now double n and watch both counts.
Double n to 200. The single loop doubles to 200 operations. The pairs loop goes from 4,950 to 19,900, about 4.0 times as many.
Double n to 400. The single loop doubles to 400 operations. The pairs loop goes from 19,900 to 79,800, about 4.0 times as many.
Double n to 800. The single loop doubles to 800 operations. The pairs loop goes from 79,800 to 319,600, about 4.0 times as many.
At n = 10 a single loop does 10 operations and the pairs loop does 45. Now double n and watch both counts.
Double n to 20. The single loop doubles to 20 operations. The pairs loop goes from 45 to 190, about 4.2 times as many.
Double n to 40. The single loop doubles to 40 operations. The pairs loop goes from 190 to 780, about 4.1 times as many.
Double n to 80. The single loop doubles to 80 operations. The pairs loop goes from 780 to 3,160, about 4.1 times as many.
Double n to 160. The single loop doubles to 160 operations. The pairs loop goes from 3,160 to 12,720, about 4.0 times as many.
At n = 1 a single loop does 1 operation and the pairs loop does 0. Now double n and watch both counts.
Double n to 2. The single loop doubles to 2 operations. The pairs loop goes from 0 to 1; there is no earlier count to compare.
Double n to 4. The single loop doubles to 4 operations. The pairs loop goes from 1 to 6, about 6.0 times as many.
Double n to 8. The single loop doubles to 8 operations. The pairs loop goes from 6 to 28, about 4.7 times as many.
Double n to 16. The single loop doubles to 16 operations. The pairs loop goes from 28 to 120, about 4.3 times as many.
